questions.title: Tidiness
questions.text: Did you keep your room tidy as a child?

questions.title: 教你新技能的人
questions.text:
Describe a person who taught you a new skill
You should say:
Who this person was
What the skill was
How you learned it
And explain how you felt about this person
questions.english:
A person who taught me a useful new skill is my supervisor. The skill I'd describe is debugging a program in a more systematic way, which is particularly relevant to my studies in AI and robotics.

Before learning it, I would sometimes change several things at once when a program didn't work. That made it difficult to know which change had helped or created another problem. My supervisor showed me how to reduce the problem to a smaller example and check one possibility at a time.

I learned by applying the method to a real task and explaining each step during our discussion. Instead of giving me the answer immediately, they asked questions that helped me see what evidence I had and what I was only assuming.

I felt grateful because the skill was useful beyond that one piece of code. It gave me a calmer way to approach unfamiliar problems. I'm quite rational, so I liked having a method I could understand and reuse. I also appreciated being treated as someone who could learn to solve the problem independently.
questions.chinese:
一位教会我实用新技能的人是我的导师。我想描述的技能，是更有条理地调试程序，它与人工智能和机器人学习尤其相关。

学会之前，程序运行出问题时，我有时会一次修改几个地方。这使我很难判断哪项修改起了作用，又是哪项引出了新问题。导师教我把问题缩小到更简单的例子，一次检查一种可能性。

我通过把方法用于具体任务，并在讨论时解释每一步来学习。导师没有马上给答案，而是提问，让我区分手里的证据与仅仅作出的假设。

我感到感激，因为这项技能不只对那段代码有用，也让我更冷静地处理陌生问题。我比较理性，因此喜欢能理解并重复使用的方法。我也很欣赏导师把我当成能学会独立解决问题的人。
pending: 导师教过调试、具体错误和指导过程均为候选；不要登记为已发生或已掌握的技能

questions.title: 不喜欢的电影
questions.text:
Describe a movie/film you don’t like
You should say:
When you watched it
Where you watched it
What it was about
And explain why don’t like it
questions.english:
A film I didn't like was one of the Transformers films. I watched it at home on my computer during a weekend, because the idea of robots was connected with an interest I already had.

The film was mainly about large robots and conflicts between different groups. There were a lot of action scenes and impressive visual effects. Those parts looked exciting, but they weren't enough to keep me interested throughout the whole story.

What I didn't like was that the action sometimes seemed more important than the characters' reasons for doing things. I found it harder to care about the events when I didn't feel a clear connection between the characters and the consequences of their choices.

I don't think a film has to be completely realistic to be enjoyable. I watch Japanese anime, so I'm comfortable with imaginative worlds. But I prefer the story to have some internal logic and give me a reason to care. For me, the film matched my interest in robots but didn't fully match my taste in storytelling.
questions.chinese:
我不喜欢的一部电影是《变形金刚》系列中的一部。一个周末，我在家用电脑观看，因为机器人的概念与我原有的兴趣相关。

电影主要讲大型机器人与不同阵营之间的冲突。有很多动作场面和令人印象深刻的视觉效果。这些部分看起来精彩，但不足以让我始终对整个故事感兴趣。

我不喜欢的是，动作有时似乎比人物做事情的理由更重要。如果人物与选择后果之间缺少清晰联系，我就更难关心剧情。

我认为电影不必完全写实才能好看。我看日本动漫，因此能接受有想象力的世界，但更希望故事有内部逻辑，并让我有理由关心它。对我来说，这部电影符合机器人兴趣，却并不完全符合我对叙事的偏好。
pending: 具体影片、观看时间地点、喜恶和评价是候选；动漫兴趣与机器人方向已确认

questions.title: 学习并喜欢历史的人
questions.text: Do you think people should learn ancient history before learning modern history?
questions.english: Learning ancient history first can provide useful background, especially when later institutions developed from earlier ones. But a strict order isn't always necessary. A modern event may interest students and lead them to explore its older roots. I think a clear timeline and links between periods matter more than requiring everyone to begin with the oldest material.
questions.chinese: 先学古代史能提供背景，尤其后来的制度源自早期制度。但严格顺序不总必要。现代事件可能吸引学生，促使探索更早根源。我认为清晰时间线和时期联系，比要求所有人从最古老材料开始更重要。

questions.text: Is it important to learn how people in the past lived their lives?
questions.english: Yes, it shows that history is about real people, not just rulers and wars. Understanding their daily challenges can make past events easier to relate to. questions.text: How do children learn history before they attend school?

questions.title: 教你新技能的人
questions.text: Why is self-discipline important when learning a new skill?
questions.english: A new skill usually requires repeated practice after the first excitement has faded. Self-discipline helps people continue when progress is slow or mistakes become frustrating. For example, learning to code involves testing and fixing problems, not just watching a tutorial. Regular, manageable practice builds ability more reliably than one long session followed by several weeks of doing nothing.
questions.chinese: 新技能通常需要在最初兴奋消退后反复练习。自律帮助在进步缓慢或错误令人烦时坚持。例如学编程需要测试、修问题，而非只看教程。规律、可管理练习，比一次长练后数周不练更可靠地建立能力。

questions.title: 教你新技能的人
questions.text: What are the differences between learning from a teacher and learning by oneself?
questions.english: A teacher can provide structure, spot mistakes, and explain difficult ideas in a different way. Independent learning gives people flexibility and lets them follow their own interests. The risk is getting stuck without knowing what is wrong. questions.text: How do adults learn a new skill?

questions.text: How can parents and teachers teach children new skills?

questions.title: 不喜欢的电影
questions.text: Do people’s movie preferences change as they get older?
questions.english: Preferences often change as people gain different experiences, but they don't change in one fixed direction. A teenager may enjoy excitement and later become more interested in complex relationships or social issues. Someone else may keep loving animation throughout life. Available time matters too. I think personal development influences taste, while favourite genres can remain a lasting source of comfort.
questions.chinese: 人们经历增多时偏好常变化，但不朝单一固定方向。青少年可能喜欢刺激，后来更关心复杂关系或社会议题。另一些人一生喜欢动画。时间也重要。我认为个人发展影响品味，但喜爱类型可一直提供慰藉。
